In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for new physics beyond the standard model of particle physics.
the search for a macroscopic force, a force that acts over distances of many centimetres or even metres.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a positive signal in a sub-cm range, which is still possible in the present state-of-the-art experiments, could not yet be excluded, but is not yet expected, either.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a large neutron electric-dipole moment is expected in a supersymmetric unified model, and that the axion-mediated macroscopical force could be detected in a favorable range.

the axions, which are the lightest particles in a supersymmetric theory and the lightest particles that can be produced at the LHC in a model-independent way, are also the lightest particles whose effects could be seen by a macroscopic force experiment.
